children: delivered a better-than-feared fiscal first quarter and set FY27 profit guidance slightly above estimates, but shares are only fractionally higher in Wednesday’s premarket trading as profits continued to be undermined by higher input costs and lower volumes.

Sales were down 3% during the quarter to $4.4B, which beat expectations by $50M but reflected the impact from the divestiture of its yogurt business. Organic sales were flat on a year-over-year basis. This left General Mills’
gross margin unchanged at 33.9% and compressed the company’s adjusted gross margin by 90 basis points to 33.3%.

By segment, North American retail sales were down 7%, which includes the headwind from the yogurt divestiture. Pet sales were flat while foodservice sales in North America were up 1%. International sales increased by 4%, which includes a 1-point foreign exchange tailwind and growth in India and China.
Looking ahead to the remainder of the year, General Mills
expects capacity growth to be consistent with recent trends and below its long-term historical growth rate, largely a result of a “continued challenging consumer backdrop.”

Based on the assumption that the company expects to generate at least $750M in savings from its Holistic Margin Management productivity program, headwinds of ~9 points on operating profit and 11 points on EPS from lapping the 53rd week in FY26, normalizing corporate incentive expense, and the impact of FY26 divestitures, the company reaffirmed its FY26 targets.
This includes organic net sales to be down 1.5% to up 0.5%, adjusted operating profit down 8% to down 13%, and free cash flow conversion to be ~95% of adjusted after-tax earnings.
Additionally, adjusted EPS are expected to be between $3.00 and $3.20 per share with a midpoint of $3.10 that is above $3.07 estimates.

title: General Mills beats conservative FQ1 estimates, but higher costs weigh on profits
